- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after spikes.
- If official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, reduce forecast mean by 2–5% to account for policy-induced downward pressure.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model should not continue rising; introduce mean reversion bias toward prior 10–15d average.
- When official event count is high and supply net is negative, forecast should be slightly below historical 30d mean to reflect over-supply expectations.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not overfit to recent trend; use 18d rolling average as anchor for correction.
- For 30d forecasts with high event density and negative supply net, apply downward bias of 3–7% if true outcome deviates >5% below forecast — especially if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
